absent: Locking, preemption, interrupt and cross-processor ordering around slot allocation, arming, fault handling and user-probe copy.
Full layouts, sizes and field meanings for probe, breakpoint, trap-context and control-block structures.
Membership, encoding and maintenance of the steppable hint whitelist.
Bit-level encoding rules behind branch, system, exclusive, literal and memory-operation classification predicates.
Visibility and synchronization guarantees of instruction patching and instruction-cache maintenance beyond slot-install notes.
Runtime extents of blacklisted entry, interrupt and hypervisor ranges and behavior when symbol extent lookup fails beyond skipping the atomic check.
Lifecycle, allocation and fault behavior of user out-of-line pages, trampoline addresses and guarded-stack primitives.

findings.text: Probe decode classifies an instruction word for breakpoint handling. A no-operation request is assigned a lightweight emulation path that needs no out-of-line slot. A steppable request is approved for out-of-line execution with no handler. Recognized control-transfer forms covering conditional branches, compare and test-bit branches, address formation, direct branches with link, indirect branches and returns receive dedicated emulation without a slot. Anything else that is neither steppable nor emulated is rejected.

Steppability excludes instructions whose behavior depends on original placement or privileged state. Within system and branch class, ordinary branches, immediate and register system writes, exception generation and authenticated or plain exception returns are excluded; system register reads are excluded except for the interrupt-mask register known as DAIF; hints are allowed only through a separate whitelist predicate. Outside that class, literal-using, exclusive-access and memory-operation forms are excluded; all remaining forms are treated as steppable.

Atomic context window is 128 bytes expressed in probe-slot units. Decode outcome uses a three-valued enumeration distinguishing rejection, acceptance without out-of-line slot, and acceptance requiring a slot.

Atomicity check walks backwards over a bounded address interval. Encountering an exclusive store first means the probed address is not inside an atomic sequence; encountering an exclusive load first means it is. Exhausting the interval without either means not atomic.

Kernel probe decode gives literal loads dedicated emulation, otherwise delegates to generic probe decode, then vetoes placement inside an atomic sequence. The backward search limit is derived from the enclosing symbol extent when known, capped by the maximum atomic window; when no symbol extent is known the atomic check is skipped.

Slot-page allocator obtains one page from probe-dedicated executable memory and transitions it to read-execute-only. Allocation or permission failure yields no page and releases any partial allocation.

Out-of-line preparation installs the copied probe word followed by a single-step breakpoint in the reserved slot and records a resume address immediately after the probe site. Simulation preparation records no resume address because execution never leaves the faulting context.

Probe preparation requires word alignment and absence from exception tables. It preserves the original word, decodes it, acquires a slot only when out-of-line execution is required, and reports misaligned or unsupported or exception-table placement differently from slot exhaustion.
Arming replaces the probe site with a probe breakpoint; disarming restores the preserved original word. Removal releases any associated out-of-line slot and clears the association.

Fault handling during probing never claims faults from fully emulated probes. For single-step and re-enter states it claims a fault only when the faulting program counter equals the current probe out-of-line slot; otherwise the fault is left to normal handling. A claimed fault rewinds execution to the probe site and releases single-step state.

Blacklist setup excludes early entry, interrupt entry and hypervisor text ranges from probing. When the kernel already runs at hypervisor privilege the final hypervisor identity-map range step is skipped and prior status is returned.

Return-probe preparation saves the link register and frame pointer from the trap context and redirects the link register to a shared trampoline. The trampoline raises a breakpoint whose handler adjusts control flow, with a terminal fault marker ensuring no fall-through execution. Trampoline presence check and subsystem initialization are no-operations reporting success.

Branch emulation updates saved register and program-counter state to the architectural effect without executing the original location. Direct forms apply signed displacement; conditional and compare or test-bit forms fall through to the next location unless their predicate holds; indirect forms transfer to a register-held target; link-producing forms also update the link register; returns transfer to a register-held target with guarded-stack verification in user context.

Address formation emulation combines page or program-counter base with sign-extended immediate into the destination register and advances past the probe. Literal-load emulation reads once from program-counter-relative memory with width and sign behavior matching the load form. No-operation emulation simply advances past a single instruction.

Register helpers read and write full or low-half general registers through the trap-context accessor. Displacement helpers derive signed program-counter-relative offsets from encoded bitfields with width appropriate to each branch or load form.

User-probe analysis rejects 32-bit contexts and misaligned addresses, decodes the saved instruction, and marks emulation-only forms to skip single-stepping. Execution preparation records a sentinel fault code, redirects to the out-of-line copy and enables user single-step; normal completion restores to the instruction after the probe and disables stepping, while abort on fatal signal restores to the probe itself. Trapping is detected by sentinel mutation.

Out-of-line copy for user probes maps the destination page locally, skips cache maintenance when content is unchanged, otherwise copies and synchronizes instruction and data views over exactly the modified range.

Return-instance liveness compares stack pointer against saved stack with inclusive bound for chain calls and exclusive bound otherwise. Return-address hijack preserves the original link value, validates guarded-stack consistency when enabled and aborts with a fault signal on mismatch or access failure, otherwise installs the trampoline address.
Per-processor probe state holds the currently active probe reference, initially empty, alongside a control block tracking single-step and re-entry status.
Invalid fault marker for user-probe single-step detection is the maximum unsigned integer value.

Guarded-stack handling pushes the link value on call emulation and pops with equality check on return emulation or hijack; any access error or mismatch raises a segmentation fault and aborts architectural state update.
User-probe exception notifier takes no action and reports that the notification was not consumed.
Process support exposes a read-only-after-init stack-canary guard and a mutable power-off operation pointer.
Header guards use dedicated macros to prevent multiple inclusion of probe decode and simulation declarations; kernel-probe logging prefixes messages with a fixed kprobes subsystem tag.
System-register specifier uses mask 0x1FFFE0 and right shift 5.
